categories.name: Coding agents
categories.q: What should I use to write and edit code with an AI agent?

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.verdict: Terminal-first agent that handles multi-file changes and long tasks well. Best if you're comfortable in a CLI.
tools.price: Included with Claude paid plans; see site

tools.name: Cursor
tools.verdict: VS Code-style editor with strong agent mode and tab completion. The easiest daily driver for most builders.
tools.price: Free tier; paid plans, see site

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.verdict: Works in almost every editor and now ships a cloud coding agent. Safe default if your code is on GitHub.
tools.price: Free tier; paid plans, see site

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.verdict: OpenAI's coding agent across CLI, IDE and cloud. Good if you already pay for ChatGPT.
tools.price: Included with ChatGPT plans; see site

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.verdict: Agentic IDE with a capable assistant (Cascade). A solid Cursor alternative.

categories.name: AI app builders
categories.q: What should I use to go from prompt to a working app?

tools.name: Lovable
tools.verdict: Polished full-stack apps from chat, with Supabase built in. Best pick for non-coders shipping an MVP.

tools.name: Bolt
tools.verdict: Fast in-browser builder with a real dev environment. Great for quick prototypes you can export.

tools.name: Replit
tools.verdict: Agent plus IDE plus hosting in one place. Easiest path from idea to a deployed URL.

tools.name: v0
tools.verdict: Best-in-class React/Next.js UI generation that deploys to Vercel. Strongest for front-ends.

categories.name: Databases & backends
categories.q: What should I use for my database, auth and backend?

tools.name: Supabase
tools.verdict: Postgres plus auth, storage and realtime. The default backend for vibe-coded apps.

tools.name: Firebase
tools.verdict: Google's mature backend with great mobile SDKs. NoSQL data model takes some getting used to.

tools.name: Neon
tools.verdict: Serverless Postgres with branching. Ideal when you just need a database, not a full backend.

tools.name: Convex
tools.verdict: Reactive TypeScript backend that AI agents write well. Great for realtime apps.

categories.name: Hosting & deploy
categories.q: Where should I deploy my app?

tools.name: Vercel
tools.verdict: Best home for Next.js, with instant preview deploys. Watch usage costs at scale.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.verdict: Simple static and Jamstack hosting with built-in forms and functions.

tools.name: Cloudflare Pages
tools.verdict: Fast global edge with a generous free tier. Pairs well with Workers.

tools.name: Render
tools.verdict: Easy home for backends, workers and databases, not just static sites.

categories.name: AI APIs & models
categories.q: Which model API should my app call?

tools.name: OpenAI API
tools.verdict: Broadest ecosystem and tooling. A safe first choice for most apps.

tools.name: Anthropic API
tools.verdict: Claude models are top-tier for coding and agents. Strong pick for tool use.

tools.name: Google Gemini API
tools.verdict: Long context with a free tier in AI Studio. Great value for prototyping.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.verdict: One API key for hundreds of models. Ideal for comparing models or adding fallbacks.

tools.name: Groq
tools.verdict: Very fast inference for open models. Use it when latency matters.

categories.name: Agent frameworks
categories.q: What should I use to build my own AI agent?

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.verdict: Lightweight, well-documented primitives for tools, handoffs and tracing.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.verdict: Stateful, controllable agent graphs. More setup, but more control.

tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
tools.verdict: The TypeScript default for streaming chat and agents in web apps.

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.verdict: Quick multi-agent 'crews' with roles. Easy to start with.

tools.name: n8n
tools.verdict: Visual workflow automation with AI agent nodes, and you can self-host it.

categories.name: Best for vibe coding
categories.q: I can't code (much). What should I use to ship?

tools.name: Lovable
tools.verdict: The most beginner-friendly way to get a real app with a backend live.

tools.name: Replit
tools.verdict: Agent builds, runs and hosts it, with nothing to install.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.verdict: The step up when you outgrow builders and want to own the code.

tools.name: Bolt
tools.verdict: Fastest prompt-to-preview loop for trying ideas.

categories.name: Video
categories.q: What should I use to make AI video?

tools.name: Runway
tools.verdict: Pro-grade generation and editing tools. The creator favourite.

tools.name: Google Veo (Flow)
tools.verdict: High-quality clips with native audio. Access depends on your Google AI plan.

tools.name: Kling AI
tools.verdict: Strong motion quality at a good price for short clips.

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.verdict: Best for talking-avatar explainers and translated videos.

categories.name: Voice
categories.q: What should I use for AI voice, TTS or voice agents?

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.verdict: The most natural TTS and voice cloning, plus a voice-agent platform.

tools.name: OpenAI Realtime API
tools.verdict: Low-latency speech-to-speech for building voice agents.

tools.name: Vapi
tools.verdict: Developer platform to ship phone and voice agents quickly.

tools.name: Deepgram
tools.verdict: Fast, accurate speech-to-text and TTS APIs.
